newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France says strike would be ruinous.
newsitem.headline: Air France says strike would be ruinous.

text.p: Air France on Friday urged pilots and engineers to ignore union calls for a four-day strike next week, saying it would wipe out the entire year's profit.
Managers were instructed to maintain regular flight schedules from May 20 to 23 despite the strike call by six unions.

"The truth is that after three years of a recovery that drew on all the resources of the company, Air France could fall under the blows of a strike that would cost 100 million francs a day," Air France said in a statement.
"Four days of strike would erase the net profit forecast for the current year and any prospect for growth," it said.
Air France said Chairman Christian Blanc had sent each pilot a letter describing the financial condition of the carrier and his concerns about a "destabilisation" campaign by the unions.
Blanc is currently in China accompanying President Jacques Chirac on a trade mission.

Air France accuses the unions of stoking the conflict by calling a strike while negotiations are under way on the points of disagreement and believes many of the pilots and flight engineers oppose the strike.
"Through their presence, on the ground or in the air, each one will be able to say, 'Yes, I am fighting for the survival of Air France'," the company's statement said.
The unions say they have the crewmembers' backing and accuse Blanc of trying to blackmail the pilots.

Unions representing pilots and flight engineers at Air France and Air France Europe, the regional wing formerly known as Air Inter that is being merged into Air France, called the strike to protest against the lower wage scale for new hires.

"It's the first time in a long time that the pilots of both carriers are united and determined to take this all the way," Eric Brouwer, secretary general of the SNPL chapter at Air France, told Reuters.
The SNPL says it represents 80 percent of the cockpit crew members of Air France and half of those at Air France Europe.
It said an independent study shows the wages proposed for new pilots at the French state-owned group are lower than those paid by Lufthansa, British Airways and KLM.
Air France wants to hire 450 pilots in the next year and a half and would pay them gross starting salaries of 220,000 francs a year, a third less than what was paid to the pilots now on staff.
